Senior Technician

• Lead and undertake product performance and site testing
• Building static load tests and installing instrumentation
• Timely completion of technical work and reporting of results

• Knowledge of testing equipment and methodologies
• Able to set up equipment and conduct test methods in line with agreed RAMS
• Competent to analyse and interpret basic data
• Completion of site and test sheets

• High customer service ethic – is passionate about meeting customer expectations and improving service levels
Client focused delivery
• Put the client at the centre of all decisions that are made
• Support colleagues in achieving for the client
• Respect the knowledge of colleagues and clients
• Listen to the views and opinions of others
• Always be polite and courteous
• Contribute in a positive way
Progressive
• Look for ways to improve processes, systems, procedures, services and delivery in all roles
• Improve skills, knowledge and experience wherever possible to the mutual benefit of the client, SOCOTEC UK and the individual
• Question things which are not understood to improve individual performance and that of SOCOTEC UK
Ownership
• Take responsibility for delivering clients requirements
• Deliver tasks to the best of one’s ability at all times
• Take pride in delivering excellent service
• GCSE English / mathematics

Qualifications
To be a successful Senior Technician, you should be able to demonstrate:
• Previous experience in a similar foundations testing role
• Full manual UK driving licence

• Good practical and communication skills

Why SOCOTEC?
Join a thriving community of over 2,000 industry professionals who are passionate about making a real difference. At SOCOTEC UK, we're not just delivering services - we're shaping the future of testing, inspection, and certification across the nation.

Build a traditional career path or explore opportunities across multiple disciplines - all within SOCOTEC. Your choice, your direction.

About This Job
As part of our Group Legal Department, you will play a key role in supporting the litigation function by proactively managing a high-volume and fast-moving caseload of customer legal claims, with a particular focus on claims arising from Claims Management Companies (CMCs).
Working closely with the Head of Litigation, Legal Counsel and an Apprentice Solicitor, you will manage day-to-day case administration, ensure compliance with court deadlines and procedural requirements, prepare case documentation and support the team's strategic approach to claims handling.
The role will also provide litigation and enforcement support to the Group’s Recoveries function, assisting with matters relating to possession proceedings, receivership appointments, bankruptcy proceedings, security enforcement and recovery actions alongside our external legal panel.
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced litigation paralegal who is highly organised, detail-oriented and motivated to broaden their expertise within an in-house legal team operating in a fast-paced financial services environment.

Qualifications
Please apply if you have a good blend of the following skills and experience:
• LLB graduate or suitable paralegal qualification
• Significant experience working as a litigation paralegal, legal executive or litigation file handler.
• Strong working knowledge of the Civil Procedure Rules (CPR).
• Experience managing a substantial caseload of litigated matters.
• Experience preparing court documents, bundles and case summaries.
• Experience working within a regulated environment, preferably financial services.
• Strong drafting and written communication skills.
• Ability to analyse complex information and present findings clearly and concisely.
• Confident working with case management systems and Microsoft Office applications.
• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
• Experience dealing with CMC-driven claims or high-volume litigation.

About This Job
Why the Two Brewers?
The Two Brewers combines everything you want from a traditional country pub — great food, welcoming hospitality and plenty of character.
From hearty pub classics and our popular Sunday roasts to relaxed drinks in the beer garden, we're proud to offer our customers a genuine home-away-from-home experience.
Our kitchen already has a strong and experienced team who know their roles and understand the operation. What we're looking for now is the right leader to bring everyone together, maintain our standards and take the kitchen into its next chapter.
And with a refit planned for Period 1 next year, this is an exciting time to join the business and play an important part in what comes next.

Qualifications
What’s the opportunity?
As Kitchen Manager / Head Chef, you'll take ownership of the kitchen and be responsible for leading the team and maintaining the standards our customers expect.
You'll:
• Lead the kitchen team from the front and set clear expectations.
• Bring the team together, creating a positive, focused and high-performing kitchen culture.
• Maintain consistently high standards across food quality, presentation and service.
• Coach, motivate and develop the kitchen team.
• Ensure everyone understands their responsibilities and works effectively together.
• Take ownership of kitchen operations and ensure every service runs smoothly.
• Manage stock takes, ordering, stock rotation and wastage.
• Maintain excellent food safety, hygiene and health & safety standards.
• Monitor food costs and GP to ensure the kitchen operates commercially.
• Work closely with the General Manager and wider management team to drive the business forward.
• Ensure the kitchen is fully prepared for busy pub and hotel trade.
• Help maximise opportunities across pub dining, hotel guests and Sunday roasts.
• Lead busy services confidently and remain calm and organised under pressure.
• Bring fresh ideas and experience to help develop the food operation.
• Play a key role in preparing the team and kitchen for the upcoming refit.
This is not about coming in and changing everything for the sake of it. The team is already strong — they need an experienced leader who can bring them together, set the direction and drive the kitchen forward.
What we’re looking for
We're looking for an experienced Kitchen Manager / Head Chef who:
• Has proven experience leading a busy kitchen.
• Ideally has experience within a pub, hotel or similar food-led hospitality environment.
• Is confident taking ownership of the kitchen and leading a team.
• Leads from the front and is comfortable being hands-on during service.
• Has a firm but fair approach to leadership.
• Has strong communication and people-management skills.
• Knows how to motivate, coach and develop a kitchen team.
• Takes pride in maintaining consistently high standards.
• Has excellent knowledge of food safety, hygiene and health & safety.
• Is confident managing stock, GP, ordering, rotation and wastage.
• Is organised and able to plan effectively around busy services.
• Is commercially aware and wants to help grow the business.
• Has the experience and confidence to make decisions and set clear expectations.
• Wants to develop their career and make a genuine impact with Greene King.
Lead the team. Raise the standards. Shape what comes next.
The Two Brewers already has a strong foundation and an experienced kitchen team. Now we need someone who can provide the leadership to bring it all together.
With a busy pub and hotel operation, around 80% occupancy across 20 bedrooms and a refit on the horizon, there's plenty of opportunity for the right person to make their mark.
If you're an experienced Kitchen Manager or Head Chef who is ready to take ownership, lead from the front and drive a kitchen forward, this could be your next move.

Additional Information
And there’s plenty in it for you...
• Career development opportunities across Greene King.
• Training and development at every level, including apprenticeships.
• 33% employee discount and 15% discount for loved ones across Greene King brands.
• 50% employee and 25% loved ones discount at Greene King Inns and hotels.
• Employee Assistance Programme supporting mental health, wellbeing and financial/legal advice.
• Enhanced family-friendly maternity and paternity policies.
• Menopause Friendly Employer.
• Refer a Friend scheme – earn up to £1,500.
• Wagestream – access to your pay as you earn.
• Retail discounts, including up to 30% at Superdrug and Three Mobile.
🍽️ Bring your experience. Lead the team. Take the Two Brewers forward.
CREATING PLACES WHERE PEOPLE FEEL WELCOME, SAFE AND THAT THEY BELONG
We aim to embed inclusion into every decision we make – across our people, customers, communities, suppliers, and operations. We want to create a culture where everyone feels welcome, valued, and able to thrive.
If you're ready to lead a strong kitchen team, maintain exceptional standards and help shape the next chapter of a much-loved country pub and hotel, we'd love to hear from you.

At Nexthink, we are building a high-performing global organization where great people can do their best work. As we continue to grow across 19 countries, we are looking for a Senior Global Compensation Manager to help ensure our compensation programs are competitive, equitable, and built to scale.
This newly created role will report directly to the Chief People Officer and lead the administration and evolution of Nexthink’s global compensation framework. You will bring rigor, sound judgment, and a practical, business-minded approach to the decisions that matter most: how we reward, retain, and grow our people.
You will lead our annual compensation cycles, turn market data into clear recommendations, and partner closely with People Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Finance, Legal, and senior leaders. What You Will Own
• Own and continuously improve Nexthink’s global compensation framework, including job architecture, grade profiles, and salary bands across 19 countries.

What You Will Bring
• Significant global compensation experience in a complex, multi-country organization, including ownership of compensation frameworks, benchmarking, merit, and bonus programs.
• Hands-on experience using Workday Advanced Compensation to run compensation cycles and translate business requirements into practical workflows alongside HRIS or implementation partners.
• Bring experience identifying and implementing innovative AI-driven solutions that streamline compensation processes, generate actionable insights, and elevate stakeholder experiences.
• Strong analytical and commercial judgment. You are comfortable building compensation scenarios, maintaining geo-differentiated salary bands, and presenting clear recommendations to Finance and senior leaders.
• Experience assessing pay equity, translating findings into action, and managing remediation tracking.
• Confidence operating in a global, multi-currency environment, including the complexities of payroll and EOR arrangements.
• The ability to balance consistency with pragmatism, knowing when to apply the framework and when a thoughtful exception is needed.
• Clear, credible communication skills. You can turn complex compensation topics into straightforward guidance for People Business Partners, managers, Finance partners, and executive stakeholders.

Qualifications
• Total Rewards, Compensation, or HR Technology leadership experience — you have administered and evolved compensation frameworks, run benchmarking cycles, and managed annual merit and bonus programs at a global company
• Workday expertise in HCM and Advanced Compensation is a plus, you understand how the system is structured, can make informed design decisions alongside a technical implementation team, and can hold a Workday partner accountable to HR requirements
• A genuine track record of driving process change through technology or automation — something you built or deployed that produced measurable outcomes
• Strong analytical fluency, comfortable modelling compensation scenarios, building geo-differentiated salary band frameworks, and presenting methodology to a CFO or senior leadership team
• Ability to operate effectively in a global, multi-currency environment with payroll complexity, EOR arrangements, and multi-country data considerations
• Excellent stakeholder communication,  you can translate complex compensation and systems decisions into clear guidance for HRBPs, managers, Finance partners, and senior leadership

Based at our Energy from Waste facility in Slough, the Plant Attendant is responsible for supporting the safe, efficient, and compliant operation of the plant. • Practical knowledge of combustion processes, steam systems, or flue gas treatment is desirable.
• Experience working to strict environmental and HSE regulations.

​Do you have experience in hydrology, hydraulic modelling and flood risk assessment, and want to apply it to challenging projects in the UK and internationally?
​Would you enjoy solving complex water-related problems across infrastructure, climate resilience, water management, mining and hydropower projects?

​Your new role
​You will join our UK Water team as an experienced hydrologist and hydraulic modeller, bringing strong technical expertise and relevant consultancy or industry experience. You will apply your knowledge of hydrology, hydraulic modelling and flood risk assessment across a varied portfolio of projects. Our work ranges from UK infrastructure and development schemes to major international assignments involving climate resilience, water management, mining, hydropower and technical due diligence. Working alongside specialists from across Ramboll, you will contribute to multidisciplinary projects while continuing to develop your technical expertise, project delivery experience and client relationships. The role will suit someone who enjoys solving complex problems, critically evaluating technical information and working collaboratively across disciplines. You will also have opportunities to contribute to the continued growth and development of our hydrology and flood risk capability.

• ​Providing clear, technically robust advice to clients and multidisciplinary project teams, translating complex hydrological and modelling outputs into practical project decisions.

• ​Supporting project delivery, technical quality, proposals and client development while sharing knowledge and supporting less experienced colleagues.

• ​Practical experience of hydrological analysis and established hydraulic modelling software such as TUFLOW, Flood Modeller or HEC-RAS, together with an understanding of current UK flood hydrology methods.

• ​Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with clients and colleagues from different technical disciplines.

• ​Leaders guided by our Leadership Principles

• ​Matched pension contributions
• ​Private medical cover and life assurance

• A track record of leading with urgency and ownership with startup experience, or equivalent experience operating with startup-level speed and agility inside a larger organization.
• Strong hands-on fluency in Java, C, and TypeScript, or closely comparable languages, with the depth to make and defend architecture and technical trade-off decisions.
• Proven experience balancing the servicing of technical debt and maintenance with continued investment in innovation, protecting platform stability without slowing the pace of new development.
• Demonstrable hands-on experience applying AI to software engineering at team scale with measurable results (e.g. AI-driven code modernisation, test generation for legacy code or agentic development workflows) and an informed point of view on how AI will change both engineering and the product itself.
• Strong product instincts and the ability to translate customer and market signals into a roadmap that ties directly to growth and revenue goals. You can connect product and technology strategy to measurable customer, commercial and business outcomes, and make clear portfolio choices across competing priorities.

• A visionary streak. You don't just execute the roadmap, you shape what the department becomes and can articulate that future clearly to your team and to leadership.
• Proven people leadership: hiring, developing, and retaining strong product and engineering talent, and building a team and org structure that can scale with the business. You have built and coached leadership teams, strengthened succession, and created operating models that empower leaders while maintaining clear accountability for outcomes.

About This Job
Role Overview:
The Senior Manager – Corporate FP&A owns cash flow analysis, forecasting, and reporting for the group, and supports the Director – Corporate FP&A across consolidated financial reporting and analysis. This role is responsible for translating complex financial data into clear, actionable insights about cash generation, free cash flow conversion, and group-level P&L movements. The Senior Manager is a trusted financial communicator to senior management and internal stakeholders, helping to ensure consistency of financial narrative and quality of insights.
Key Responsibilities:
Cash Flow Analysis & Reporting - Own group cash flow analysis and reporting as the core focus of the role. Produce the monthly and quarterly cash flow reporting pack, explain movements between forecast, budget, and actuals, and make the drivers of cash generation and cash usage clear to the CFO and senior management. Build the cash bridges that connect P&L performance to cash outcomes.
Free Cash Flow & Cash Conversion - Analyze free cash flow and cash conversion across the group, including the working capital drivers behind them—DSO, DPO, unbilled and deferred revenue, collections performance, and the cash profile of the subscription base. Identify where conversion is leaking, quantify the impact, and work with commercial and operational teams to close the gap.
Cash Forecasting Process & Systems - Own and continuously improve the group cash forecast model, cadence, and controls. Set the forecasting process across entities and functions, drive accuracy through variance tracking and back-testing, and automate manual steps where the tooling allows. Maintain a single source of truth for the group's cash position and outlook.
Consolidated Financial Reporting - Support the Director – Corporate FP&A in coordinating consolidated financial reporting across the organization. Ensure consistency of data, methodology, and narrative across reporting streams. Reconcile variances, validate data quality, and drive continuous improvement in reporting processes and controls.
Business Driver Analysis & Narrative - Analyze group-level P&L movements and their cash consequences: why did ARR change? why did gross margin move? what's driving operating leverage or expense growth? and how does each of these land in cash? Articulate the business drivers (volume, pricing, mix, productivity, retention, operational efficiency) in clear, executive-ready narratives. Provide context that helps the Board and CFO understand what's sustainable vs. one-off in financial performance.
Financial Commentary Development - Develop monthly/quarterly performance narratives, financial presentations, Board commentary, and forecasting documents, with cash flow and liquidity commentary as a standing component. Coordinate across finance functions to ensure commentary is consistent, fact-based, and highlights the drivers of business performance.
Liquidity & Financial Planning - Work with treasury and operations to model the cash and liquidity impact of business decisions. Provide early warning on cash constraints, funding requirements, or opportunities for deployment.
Ad-Hoc Strategic Analysis - Support the CEO, CFO, and Strategic Finance team with rapid-turnaround analysis on strategic initiatives, business cases, market conditions, and operational performance. Build financial models that enable scenario planning and decision-making, including the cash implications of each scenario.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications, Experience and Skills:
• Demonstrable in depth experience of financial analysis/reporting, with a focus on cash flow forecasting, analysis, and reporting.
• Deep expertise in cash flow forecasting, free cash flow and cash conversion analysis, and working capital drivers.
• Experience in SaaS or high-growth software companies.
• Proven ability to translate complex financial data into clear narrative and actionable insights.
• Strong financial modeling skills in Excel, including building and maintaining cash forecast models.
• Solid grounding in consolidated financial reporting and P&L analysis.
• Excellent communication skills; ability to present financial insights to senior management and C-suite.
• Experience managing or mentoring analysts within a finance function.
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field; CPA or MBA preferred.
• A persistent nature and a willingness to understand and overcome operational challenges/obstacles.
• Ability to understand processes and challenges, and navigate them effectively.
Preferred Qualifications:
• Previous experience in a multinational technology company would be an advantage.
• Track record of improving cash conversion (DSO, DPO, unbilled and deferred revenue) in a subscription business.
• Experience automating cash forecasting or reporting in an EPM or BI tool.
• Exposure to enterprise planning tools (Oracle EPM, Adaptive Insights).
• Experience with financial controls, audit processes, and regulatory reporting.

Additional Information
We believe that coming together as a community, in person, is important for innovation, connection and fostering a sense of belonging. Our roles have the right balance of remote and in-office working to enable flexibility for managing your life along with ensuring a real connection with your colleagues and the broader IFS community.

During the two-year Training Contract, you will experience the challenging high-performance world of commercial law and gain the breadth of experience you need to emerge as a confident solicitor in England and Wales. You will have four six-month rotations, giving you the opportunity to explore the firms Global Product Groups. You will complete at least one of your seats in one of the following five Global Product Groups: Capital Markets, Debt Finance, Project Development & Finance, Restructuring & Insolvency, or Structured Finance. You may have the opportunity to undertake an international secondment, a client secondment or a split seat secondment with our Disputes team and our Pro Bono clients. Trainees receive a salary of £56,000 in their first year, £61,000 in their second year, and £150,000 as a newly qualified lawyer.

Qualifications
Our Training Contract is open to penultimate year law students, final year law and non-law students and graduates. You must be eligible to start your Training Contract in August 2029 and/or February 2030. Your intake may be decided by the recruitment team. For further information on eligibility, please refer to our FAQs on our website. You must have achieved or be on track to achieve a 2:1 or above in your undergraduate degree.
If you are applying for our London Training Contract and you have not studied an England and Wales qualifying law degree, then you will need to complete the PGDL prior to joining us as a Trainee. Please note that if you are a Scots or Irish law student or graduate you may be required to do elements of the PGDL. All Future Trainees will also need to complete the SQE prior to joining us as a Trainee, this is irrespective of whether you have already completed the LPC. All Future Trainees who have already completed the SQE will still need to complete the Clifford Chance Plus Programme, which is a bespoke course designed by our lawyers in collaboration with the University of Law. Both the PGDL and SQE are funded by Clifford Chance and we will provide a maintenance grant to use during your studies. More details can be found on our website here. If you have already completed the PGDL, you need to have achieved a commendation (60% or more) overall and achieved a completion (a pass or better) on all modules at first attempt. If you have already completed the SQE, you need to have passed all modules on first attempt.

Additional Information
How to apply:
• Complete the online application form.
• Take the Clifford Chance Immersive Online Assessment and Watson Glaser critical reasoning test.
• If you pass the Watson Glaser test, your application form will be reviewed by the recruitment team.
• Successful candidates at application review will be invited to a recorded video interview.
If you are successful at the video interview stage, you will be invited for an in-person assessment day which is typically no more than 3-4 hours in duration. It will consist of a case study exercise (inclusive of a written exercise), a combined case study and competency-based interview with a Partner and Senior Associate, and a group exercise.
Who you will work with:
At the start of each seat, you will receive specialised training in that sector and a dedicated supervisor. Throughout your Training Contract, you will be closely supported by the Early Talent Development team, your Supervisor, Resource Manager, and your Monitoring Partner. They will all be available to act as mentors and advisors on a full range of subjects, but it will be up to you to make the most of this support network. You will have access to learning and development support from the Clifford Chance Academy, arguably the legal sector's leading in-house learning and development facility.
What you will do:
Whilst your experience in each seat will be very different, in all of them you will develop your legal and business skills, gain insight into our high-profile clients, and enhance your commercial awareness. The tasks you undertake could include drafting and proofing documents, conducting due diligence on a client's acquisition target, attending client meetings, preparing documents for a court hearing, researching titles and leases on a real estate portfolio, or creating a data room ahead of a major transaction. You may even run some smaller transactions for our clients These are just some examples of the breadth of work you may be involved in as a trainee.
Your career experience so far:

G4S (now part of Allied Universal) is the largest secure solutions company in the world and one of Britain's top Employers. •
Meet or exceed personal and team productivity targets.
•
Carry out any other duties that are deemed reasonable.
•
Undertake training activities as required.

Operate in receipt and dispatch function, dealing with both internal and/or external customers, including responsibility for accurate loading/unloading
•
Ensure Standard and Local Operating Procedures are adhered to at all times.

The packing by hand of bulk and part coin orders by delivery route into appropriate cages and crates and securing and sealing.

Use of Viper track and trace system to ensure integrity of audit trail.

Coin depositing by Financial Institution through the appropriate cash management computer system; identifying discrepancies and escalating to line management.
•
Ensure all working cages are secured at the end of shift.
•
Ensure all company security procedures are adhered to at all times.
•
Observe all Health & Safety requirements whilst within the coin centre.

Complete necessary paperwork and/or the appropriate cash management systems accurately within the department.

An appropriate level of numeracy is also very important
•
You will need to be confident following specific procedures and instructions
•
You must also be able to work to tight deadlines
•

Licensed in the use of powered machinery (or able to obtain licence)

Ability to work with volume counting machinery

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/asos/7440001513.description_excerpt:
About This Job
We’re looking for a Senior Engineering Lead to build and lead our AI engineering team in FinTech and Fashion Tech at ASOS, the technology teams behind Finance and our Commercial, Buying and Merchandising functions. This is a hands on engineering leadership role. You’ll line manage and grow a team of AI Engineers who build, deploy and support automation and agentic AI solutions, and you’ll still write code yourself when it counts.
The teams we support run some of the highest volume, most process heavy operations in the business, from accounts payable, reconciliation and expenses in Finance, through to range planning, trading, stock and supplier data on the commercial side. There is real scope to take repetitive manual work off people, speed up decisions and give them their time back.
This is a delivery role rather than a strategy one. ASOS has a central AI team who own our AI policy, framework, approved tooling and guardrails, and you won’t be setting that direction for the wider business. You’ll build for the teams we support within it, working closely with the central team and our AI centre of excellence to stay aligned. Within that remit you own delivery end to end, from understanding the problem through to supporting what goes live, including the agents already running today.
Key Responsibilities
Leading and Growing the Engineering Team
• Line manage a team of AI Engineers, covering objectives, one to ones, development, career progression and performance.
• Grow the team. Hire well, onboard new engineers properly, and build the skills we need as the work changes.
• Coach and mentor through design reviews, pairing and code review, and give honest feedback that helps people improve.
• Look after the health of the team, balancing workload and capacity so people are on the right work and not carrying too much.
Technical Direction and Engineering Standards
• Own the technical direction for the team, including the architecture, reusable patterns and reference solutions we build from.
• Set and hold the engineering standards, covering code quality, testing, evaluation, peer review, CI/CD and secure by default habits.
• Make the build or buy calls for your team, and keep an eye on running cost, performance and technical debt.
Building and Running AI Solutions
• Stay hands on. Lead from the front by writing code, prototyping, unblocking your team and picking up the hardest builds yourself.
• Design, build and ship production ready agentic AI and automation solutions: agents that can plan, reason, use tools, retrieve information, act across our systems and hand back to a person when they should.
• Build the integrations that make agents genuinely useful, connecting them to platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations, ReconArt, Concur, ServiceNow and our data platform, and use retrieval augmented generation and grounding so solutions are accurate against real business data.
Owning Delivery
• Own delivery for the team. Plan and prioritise the backlog, manage capacity and dependencies, and move work quickly from proof of concept into production.
• Run the team’s work through Azure DevOps and follow the wider ASOS delivery process, including governance, change control and release cadence.
• Own the agents and automations already live, put proper operational foundations in place including monitoring, alerting, runbooks and clear ownership, and lead incident response when things go wrong.
Working with Stakeholders and the Central AI Team
• Get out into Finance, Commercial, Buying and Merchandising to understand how people really work and what is genuinely worth automating, and explain the options back in plain language.
• Build inside the policies, approved tooling and guardrails the central AI team sets, and be our main point of contact with them and the AI centre of excellence so we stay aligned.
• Track and evidence the benefit delivered, whether that is time saved, manual effort removed or cycle times cut, and report progress and risks honestly to senior stakeholders.

About This Job
Self-employed / No-contract / Temporary / Part-time / Shift-work
https://flex.amazon.co.uk/recruiting-cities/london per hour* based on delivering a number of parcels across an estimated length of time (referred to as a block).
Deliveries will be collected from the depot in Wimbledon and will be made to the surrounding areas.
Deliver packages locally and get paid weekly. Flexible hours. Be your own boss.
What is Amazon Flex?
It's simple! You use your own vehicle and your smartphone to deliver packages locally for Amazon as a way of earning extra money weekly to move you closer to your goals. Schedule a delivery block and start delivering parcels as little or as often as you like.
Who can deliver for Amazon Flex?
To become a Delivery Driver you need a valid UK driving licence and a vehicle. Currently the only available delivery options are for owners of a 4-door car or van.You will need to be entitled to work in the UK and pass a background and criminal record check which includes, but is not limited to, a review of driving licence records. Current Amazon employees are not eligible to be Delivery Partners.
How do I sign up?
Grab your mobile and visit the Amazon Flex website to download the app for iPhone or Android. After the download, the app guides you step-by-step through the onboarding process. Once you have passed your background and criminal record check, you will be able to schedule a block and start delivering smiles!
How long are the blocks?
Blocks vary in length, from 1 to 5 hours, depending on the delivery service you support. For example, 1-hour and 2-hour blocks are available for Prime Now deliveries, where customers receive their deliveries within a few hours of making their order. About This Job
The future role holder can be located in our offices in Norwich or Cambridge
Are you excited by the prospect of delivering major infrastructure that will support the needs of millions of people? We are seeking someone who understands the complexity of Development Consent Orders (DCOs) and relevant secondary consents for this leadership position. This is an opportunity to take a visible, hands-on role in complex infrastructure delivery, working at the point where consented design, stakeholder commitments, environmental obligations and construction reality come together.
If this sounds like you, or you are curious to learn more, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our UK Environment and Health team as our new Environment and Consents Manager and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.
Your new role
As an Environment and Consents Manager, you will play a key role in supporting the discharge of DCO Requirements, identifying and managing secondary consents, and maintaining environmental compliance for major infrastructure and development projects. You will help clients and contractors understand, secure, discharge and comply with the consents, permits, licences, approvals and environmental commitments required to move projects from planning and pre-construction into construction delivery.
This will be a predominantly site-based role, working closely with contractors, construction teams, designers, environmental specialists, planners, legal advisers, local authorities, regulators, statutory bodies and community-facing teams to identify consenting risks, coordinate submissions, support the discharge of DCO Requirements and secondary consents, and maintain clear evidence of compliance. The role will suit someone who enjoys being close to delivery, solving practical problems and using stakeholder engagement to help project teams keep works moving in line with consented commitments.
You will be part of a collaborative UK team with access to Ramboll’s wider technical expertise across impact assessment, ecology, water, landscape, air quality, noise, climate, sustainability, health and safety, social value and environmental management. You will have the opportunity to lead consenting workstreams, support multi-disciplinary bids and help shape practical, proportionate solutions for complex infrastructure and development projects.
Your key responsibilities will be:
• Lead the management of DCO requirements, secondary consents and environmental compliance for infrastructure and development projects, ensuring all legal and planning obligations are met on time.
• Develop and maintain discharge trackers, consent registers, application packs and evidence bundles, and prepare stakeholder briefings, meeting notes and action plans.
• Engage regulators, statutory consultees, local and highways authorities, contractors and technical specialists to resolve consenting issues, drive approvals and maintain programme confidence.
• Review and interpret environmental permissions (DCOs, TWAOs, permits, licences, CEMPs, etc.) and translate commitments into practical controls, surveys and assurance checks.
• Provide on-site support to contractors and delivery teams, coordinating cross-disciplinary inputs and securing robust close-out evidence for compliance.
• Advise on design, land, methodology and programme changes, embedding consenting requirements, seasonal constraints and mitigation measures into project schedules, and assessing associated risks and opportunities.
• Contribute to proposals, budgets and delivery plans for consenting and environmental management commissions, and mentor junior colleagues through technical guidance and quality review.
About you
• Relevant experience in DCO Requirement discharge, secondary consents, environmental permitting, environmental management, infrastructure delivery or a related field.
• Good understanding of UK environmental legislation, consenting routes and regulatory processes, ideally with experience working with local authorities, the Environment Agency, Natural England, highways authorities or other consent-granting bodies.
• Experience preparing and managing consent applications, discharge and compliance trackers, environmental management plans, commitments registers and supporting evidence packs.
• Confident working on site with contractors and construction teams, providing clear, practical advice on DCO requirements, environmental controls, permit conditions and compliance evidence.
• Ability to interpret technical information quickly and communicate it clearly through high-quality written outputs, stakeholder briefings and day-to-day engagement with clients, delivery teams and external stakeholders.
• Strong organisational and coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple actions, interfaces and deadlines in a programme-driven environment.
• Degree-qualified in environmental science, environmental management, planning, geography, engineering or a related discipline.
• Collaborative and delivery-focused, with a willingness to spend most of the week on site in Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire or Suffolk, alongside travel to client offices and other project locations as required.
What we can offer you
• Commitment to your development
• Leaders guided by our Leadership Principles
• A culture that welcomes you as the unique person you are
• Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects
• The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company
• Flexible work environment
• 27 days annual leave plus bank holidays
• Matched pension contributions
• Private medical cover and life assurance
Ready to join us?
Please submit your application and CV online. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.
We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.
Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll
Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll employs more than 18,000 people globally across 35 countries. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, Management Consulting, and Architecture & Landscape. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we help shape the societies of tomorrow.

• Produce a practical roadmap for future implementation and investment;

Comfortable and able to work quickly to meet structured targets

About This Job
About Our Team:
At AECOM, our water scientists in the Water Environment team, work for clients from across the public and private sectors including UK Water Companies, the Environment Agency, Highways England, Natural England, Water Utilities, Rivers and Wildlife Trusts in the UK, as well as commercial developers and overseas clients. We are also involved in major ongoing projects such as the HS2 and as a team are responsible for coordinating & leading water environment chapters in Environmental Statements as well as coordinating Water Framework Directive (WFD) assessments
The Water Environment team spans office locations across the UK, Ireland and France. The advertised position is to join the Basingstoke, Bristol or Croydon-based team from January 2027 onwards.
The role will involve groundwater investigative studies (e.g. baseline studies, conceptual site model preparation, compilation and analysis of water level and water quality data, environmental compliance), groundwater exploration and development field studies (e.g. drilling supervision, borehole specification and design, water level and quality monitoring, step test and pumping test supervision) and groundwater impact assessment studies (e.g. baseline studies, constraint identification (both in field and desk based), catchment delineation, hydrogeological impact assessment, recommendation of mitigation measures).
Here’s what you’ll do:
An integral part of your role will be writing reports and undertaking analysis, interpretation and presentation of data. You’ll also be involved in field work such as water feature surveys, borehole drilling supervision, pumping test supervision and environmental monitoring. Your initial focus on gaining site experience will gradually transition into taking more responsibility for interpreting data and preparing reports.
Your responsibilities will include:

AI-Enabled Security Operations

You'll work across a diverse range of scientific and operational teams, each with different processes, priorities and accreditation requirements. You'll need to understand those differences, build strong relationships and find practical solutions that maintain compliance without creating unnecessary barriers.
We're looking for someone who can turn “we can't do that” into “how can we make that work?”
You'll bring the technical credibility to challenge existing practices, the judgement to manage risk proportionately, and the people skills to bring others with you. Alongside maintaining a robust quality framework, you'll have the opportunity to improve systems, simplify processes and make better use of technology.
If you enjoy solving complex problems, influencing change and helping teams find better ways of working, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.
What you'll be doing
•
Lead quality across the business: Act as a trusted quality partner to scientific and operational teams, providing expert guidance on accreditation, compliance, risk and continuous improvement.
•
Own and strengthen the QMS: Maintain and develop our Quality Management System, ensuring it remains effective, compliant and fit for purpose across different areas of the business.
•
Drive accreditation and compliance: Interpret ISO/IEC 17025 requirements, support the ongoing development of our accredited quality framework and deputise for the ISO 17025 Quality Manager as required.
•
Lead audits and investigations: Manage audit activity, root cause investigations, non-conformances, corrective actions, risk assessments and change control, ensuring actions address underlying issues and deliver lasting improvements.
•
Turn challenges into solutions: Work collaboratively with teams to resolve quality issues, balance compliance requirements with operational needs and influence decisions at all levels.
•
Improve systems and processes: Lead improvement initiatives, identify opportunities to simplify processes and support the development of our electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), including digital tools and SharePoint-based solutions.
•
Coordinate projects and stakeholders: Work with internal teams and external accreditation bodies to plan and deliver accreditation activities, manage competing priorities and achieve successful outcomes.
•
Develop capability: Coach and support colleagues, helping embed a positive quality culture and build confidence in quality practices across the organisation.

Qualifications
You'll be an experienced quality professional with a strong understanding of laboratory accreditation and the confidence to operate independently in a varied, fast-moving environment.
You'll have:
•
Substantial experience managing or leading a Quality Management System within an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited laboratory environment.
•
A strong understanding of accreditation requirements and how to translate them into effective, practical working processes.
•
Experience leading audits, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, risk assessments and change control.
•
The ability to assess quality risks, prioritise effectively and focus on improvements that deliver meaningful results.
•
Experience improving quality systems, processes or ways of working, ideally including eQMS, SharePoint or other digital quality tools.
•
Strong project management and organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate activities across multiple teams and stakeholders.
•
Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively, build credibility and bring people along with you.
You'll be someone who:
Finds solutions, not just problems. You can challenge a decision while working collaboratively to find a compliant way forward.
Builds relationships and credibility. You understand different perspectives and adapt your approach to the people and teams you're supporting.
Enjoys variety. You're comfortable switching between different scientific disciplines, operational challenges and competing priorities.
Improves how things work. You question established practices, identify opportunities to simplify and turn ideas into practical improvements.
Brings structure to ambiguity. You're proactive, comfortable working autonomously and able to create clarity where processes or responsibilities aren't always clearly defined.
Makes quality meaningful. You help colleagues understand not just what is required, but why it matters and how to achieve it effectively.

https://flex.amazon.co.uk/recruiting-cities/london per hour* based on delivering a number of parcels across an estimated length of time (referred to as a block).
Deliveries will be collected from the depot in Croydon and will be made to the surrounding areas.
Deliver packages locally and get paid weekly. Flexible hours. Be your own boss.
What is Amazon Flex?
It's simple! You use your own vehicle and your smartphone to deliver packages locally for Amazon as a way of earning extra money weekly to move you closer to your goals. Schedule a delivery block and start delivering parcels as little or as often as you like.
Who can deliver for Amazon Flex?
To become a Delivery Driver you need a valid UK driving licence and a vehicle. Currently the only available delivery options are for owners of a 4-door car or van.You will need to be entitled to work in the UK and pass a background and criminal record check which includes, but is not limited to, a review of driving licence records. Current Amazon employees are not eligible to be Delivery Partners.
How do I sign up?
Grab your mobile and visit the Amazon Flex website to download the app for iPhone or Android. After the download, the app guides you step-by-step through the onboarding process. Once you have passed your background and criminal record check, you will be able to schedule a block and start delivering smiles!
How long are the blocks?
Blocks vary in length, from 1 to 5 hours, depending on the delivery service you support. For example, 1-hour and 2-hour blocks are available for Prime Now deliveries, where customers receive their deliveries within a few hours of making their order. However, for https://www.amazon.co.uk/ deliveries, the area served is larger. In those cases, it's not feasible to have 1-hour or 2-hour blocks and the available blocks are 4-hour and 5-hour.
Money Matters. Know your earnings.
When you schedule a delivery block, you'll know estimated duration and your total payments all before your delivery block begins. You can build your own schedule, there are delivery blocks available seven days a week. However, the available delivery blocks may fluctuate week-to-week and are not guaranteed.
Adjust your work not your life.
Perhaps you have a job but want to supplement your income. Or maybe you are already a delivery driver and want something to keep you busy on the quieter days. Whatever your situation Amazon Flex can offer you the freedom and flexibility to be your own boss and earn extra cash on your own schedule.
No matter what drives you, Amazon Flex helps you get there. Sign-up today.
* Earnings estimates are based on delivering a number of packages across an estimated length of time (referred to as a block), completed while driving a standard motorised vehicle. Should Amazon Flex introduce blocks eligible to be delivered using scooters or other alternative modes of transportation, different rates may apply. We aim to ensure that the number of packages you are assigned to deliver within your block is realistic, taking into account congestion and the primary requirement to drive safely.

Deliveries will be collected from the depot in Wimbledon and will be made to the surrounding areas.
Deliver packages locally and get paid weekly. Flexible hours. Be your own boss.
What is Amazon Flex?
It's simple! You use your own vehicle and your smartphone to deliver packages locally for Amazon as a way of earning extra money weekly to move you closer to your goals. Schedule a delivery block and start delivering parcels as little or as often as you like.
Who can deliver for Amazon Flex?
To become a Delivery Driver you need a valid UK driving licence and a vehicle. Currently the only available delivery options are for owners of a 4-door car or van.You will need to be entitled to work in the UK and pass a background and criminal record check which includes, but is not limited to, a review of driving licence records. Current Amazon employees are not eligible to be Delivery Partners.
How do I sign up?
Grab your mobile and visit the Amazon Flex website to download the app for iPhone or Android. After the download, the app guides you step-by-step through the onboarding process. Once you have passed your background and criminal record check, you will be able to schedule a block and start delivering smiles!
How long are the blocks?
Blocks vary in length, from 1 to 5 hours, depending on the delivery service you support. For example, 1-hour and 2-hour blocks are available for Prime Now deliveries, where customers receive their deliveries within a few hours of making their order. However, for https://www.amazon.co.uk/ deliveries, the area served is larger. In those cases, it's not feasible to have 1-hour or 2-hour blocks and the available blocks are 4-hour and 5-hour.
Money Matters. Know your earnings.
When you schedule a delivery block, you'll know estimated duration and your total payments all before your delivery block begins. You can build your own schedule, there are delivery blocks available seven days a week. However, the available delivery blocks may fluctuate week-to-week and are not guaranteed.
Adjust your work not your life.
Perhaps you have a job but want to supplement your income. Or maybe you are already a delivery driver and want something to keep you busy on the quieter days. Whatever your situation Amazon Flex can offer you the freedom and flexibility to be your own boss and earn extra cash on your own schedule.
No matter what drives you, Amazon Flex helps you get there. Sign-up today.
* Earnings estimates are based on delivering a number of packages across an estimated length of time (referred to as a block), completed while driving a standard motorised vehicle. Should Amazon Flex introduce blocks eligible to be delivered using scooters or other alternative modes of transportation, different rates may apply. We aim to ensure that the number of packages you are assigned to deliver within your block is realistic, taking into account congestion and the primary requirement to drive safely.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/dpdgroupuk1/744.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The Role
We’re looking for someone to take the wheel and own a designated local route. You aren’t just moving boxes; you’re the final boss of the delivery game, ensuring every parcel hits its destination with 10/10 service. With around 40 - 50 stops a day, you’ll be the ultimate problem-solver, navigating your community and making life easier for our customers. Your role is vital in providing a service that genuinely makes a difference to our customers.
The Role Breakdown
• Drive the Vibe: Get behind the wheel of a 7.5 Tonne vehicle. You’ll be cruising local routes, keeping it safe, professional, and efficient.
• Master the Tech: No paper maps here. You’ll use our industry-leading Saturn handheld devices. It’s basically your mission control for tracking progress, managing deliveries, and staying ahead of the game.
• The Main Character Energy: You’re the friendly face our customers see every day. Whether it’s a quick "hello" or a helpful drop-off, your energy defines the DPD experience.
• The Hustle: You’ll be loading and unloading parcels, using high-end gear like sack barrows and hand trucks to handle the heavy lifting safely. Think of it as a paid workout while you're on the move.
If you’re someone who loves autonomy, stays tech-savvy, and enjoys being out in the real world rather than stuck behind a screen, this is your lane.

Qualifications
What You Bring
• The Essentials: A valid 7.5 Tonne (C1) licence and DQC/CPC accreditation.
• Experience: Ideally 6 months recent driving experience handling 7.5 Tonne vehicles.
• Vibe: You’re professional, approachable, and thrive in a fast-paced environment.
• Fitness: You’re physically active and comfortable with the lifting involved in the job.
• Values: You care about doing a good job and treat customers and colleagues with respect.
Ready to start? If you have the drive and the DPD DNA to succeed, we want to hear from you.

About This Job
Boost your career at the absolute frontier of aerospace technology by joining our TEMPEST team, helping to deliver the UK’s 6th generation fighter aircraft. As an engineer on this critical multi-national project, you will actively design, build, and integrate the next generation of combat air capability. You will collaborate with industry-leading minds to pioneer breakthroughs in artificial intelligence, digital model based engineering, and truly next-generation computing. This is a rare opportunity to see your innovations directly shape the future of global defence, work with cutting-edge technologies, and fast-track your professional development on one of the most ambitious engineering ventures of the century.
In this role you will:
• Contribute to the software architecture and design of mission systems
• Support software integration and test/V&V activities
• Contribute to Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) initiatives
• Develop technologies that will shape combat aviation for decades to come.
• Work with world-leading engineers across industry, government and academia.
• Contribute to sovereign UK defence capability and international collaboration.

Qualifications
Successful candidates should ideally possess:
• Degree level education or equivalent in a relevant engineering discipline.
• Demonstrable experience of architecting, designing and delivering software solutions
• Competency in at least one of C, C++, Python or Ada
• Demonstrated high levels of motivation, integrity, and professionalism
• Flexibility, innovation, and commitment to delivery in fast-paced environments
• Knowledge of UML and/or DO-178C is advantageous but not necessary
• Experience working with or familiarity with AI/ML models is preferred.

Additional Information
This role has a salary of between £36,000 and £45,000 plus our flexible benefits package.
We are open to this role being spent with time working from home and in the office (hybrid - typically 3 days working in office) on a weekly basis or fully in our offices.
We pride ourselves in being a great place to work with a shared sense of purpose, offering impressive benefits:
• A compressed nine-day fortnight and compressed hours - which means every other Friday off.
• A personalized career development plan, alongside regular progress reviews - supporting and valuing your progression within the Company.
• A flexible working environment where your contributions are recognized and rewarded with flexible benefits
We believe in maintaining a diverse workplace - inclusive of beliefs, cultural background, job experiences, thoughts and ideas. If who we are and what we do resonates with you, we welcome you to join our inclusive team!
Our success is fuelled by our colleagues and the wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills they bring to the Company.
We are a Disability Confident Employer, as such we offer an interview to disabled people who meet the minimum criteria for the job.
Please email disabilityconfident@gd-ms.uk if you would like your application to be considered under the DC Scheme.
All successful/appointed applicants must be able to obtain a level of UK Security clearance that is appropriate for the role and undertake suitable Right to work checks.
Every application matters to us. We want you to know that each application we receive is reviewed by a real person—not just an algorithm. Our screening questions are also carefully considered to help us understand your experience and fit for the role.
We appreciate the time you take to apply.

About This Job
Bosch Manufacturing Co-Intelligence is seeking a highly motivated Account Executive to accelerate the adoption of Industrial AI and Manufacturing Intelligence solutions across the UK manufacturing sector. This customer-facing role is focused on acquiring new customers, developing strategic accounts, and driving sustainable revenue growth.
As a trusted advisor to manufacturing leaders, you will help companies unlock operational excellence, improve productivity, and accelerate digital transformation through AI-powered manufacturing solutions.
Key Responsibilities:
• Drive new business development and revenue growth across small, medium-sized, and large manufacturing enterprises.
• Build, manage, and advance a qualified sales pipeline from prospect identification through contract negotiation and deal closure.
• Lead complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales cycles for Industrial AI, Manufacturing Intelligence, and digital transformation solutions.
• Apply consultative and value-based selling methodologies to develop compelling business cases and measurable ROI propositions.
• Establish and maintain relationships across Operations, Manufacturing, Engineering, Plant Management, Digital, and IT functions.
• Collaborate closely with Sales Leadership, Solution Consultants, and Customer Success teams to develop winning account strategies.
• Maintain rigorous pipeline management, forecasting accuracy, and CRM discipline, ensuring clear visibility of opportunities, risks, and next actions.
• Identify emerging customer needs, new use cases, and expansion opportunities related to AI adoption, smart manufacturing, and operational excellence.
• Represent Bosch Manufacturing Co-Intelligence at customer engagements, industry events, campaigns, and partner activities as a trusted brand ambassador.

Qualifications
Education:
• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in business, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, Manufacturing, or a related discipline.
Experience & Knowledge
• Proven track record of successfully selling enterprise SaaS solutions within Industrial Software, Manufacturing Technology, AI, IIoT, Automation, Digital Transformation, or related markets.
• At least 5 years+ experience managing complex B2B sales opportunities involving multiple stakeholders and extended decision-making processes.
• Strong understanding of cloud topics, Industrial AI manufacturing operations, production processes, industrial automation, and Industry 4.0 initiatives.
• Demonstrated excellence in pipeline management, sales forecasting, CRM discipline, and target achievement.
• Proficiency in structured sales methodologies such as Challenger Sales, Value Selling, MEDDICC, or similar frameworks would be a plus.
Skills & Working Style:
• Strong communication, presentation and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to engage confidently with senior executives and operational leaders.
• Collaborative and team-oriented mindset with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams.
• Commercially driven, self-motivated, and execution-focused while maintaining strategic account perspective.
Travel
• Willingness to travel across the UK and occasionally internationally as required for customer engagements, industry events, and internal meetings.
Language:
• Excellent English communication skills, both written and verbal.

Additional Information
On offer is a competitive salary and pension contributions. With a great package of benefits including annual bonus, a health cash plan, life assurance, and other discounted benefits. We will also provide many opportunities for personal and professional development.
This role is offered on an 12-month fixed term contract, subject to business needs, performance, and organisational requirements, there may be the opportunity for the contract to be extended beyond the initial term.
Hybrid working, travel to the Denham office required
Full time 37.5 hrs
This position has been internally evaluated as an SL1
We welcome applications from a range of candidates but please note that to apply for this position you must have the right to live and work in the UK from the start date of the role and for the duration of your employment.

As a Retail Customer Service Manager, you will play an important role in the Entain family, delivering top customer service and driving standards daily. About This Job
The role
Clifford Chance's real estate team operates at the very top end of the real estate sector devising innovative, bespoke and commercial solutions for our clients where real estate is the core asset.  We work across the entire property life cycle advising a full range of market participants on some of their biggest and/or most challenging transactions.
Life is never boring in this tight knit, collegiate team and a role at Clifford Chance will expose you to the breadth of the real estate industry's leading players and their most complex and challenging matters.
You will be advising on everything from direct and indirect investments into pan-European portfolios and single assets in the hottest asset classes in the market (such as data centres, healthcare, logistics, operational real estate, student accommodation, PRS, BTR, life sciences and film studios to name a few), as well as hotels, offices and retail, to iconic real estate developments in London, urban regeneration projects, real estate joint ventures, real estate M&A/private equity and financings.  We intentionally do not target commodity volume-based transactions so you will have a genuine opportunity to further develop your legal skills, commercial acumen and understanding of real estate as an asset class as well being fully embedded in strategic client relationships.  Many of our clients' deals are off market where they are trying out new approaches and asset classes - this first mover approach naturally forms a bond as we take a team within a team approach.
Our London real estate team is part of a market leading global real estate sector team with over 500 lawyers operating across UK, Europe, Asian, the Middle East and US and given the very international nature of  our clients and the work we do for them, this means you will be working with our global network not just your immediate colleagues in the UK and will have the benefit of all the resources that a large international firm brings.
We pride ourselves on being inclusive, non-hierarchical and a genuine meritocracy.
Who you will work with
The prominence of our Real Estate team makes this an unrivalled opportunity for high calibre candidates who wish to develop their careers in a fast-moving and critical sector.  We aim to be the market leader in the sectors and asset classes in which we operate and look for lawyers who share this ambition.
As part of our team, you will work closely with the firm's market leading Construction; Corporate; Private Equity; Energy & Infrastructure, Environment and Planning; Property Litigation; Real Estate Finance and Real Estate Tax Groups in both the UK and across our other offices in the network.  Our clients are primarily financial investors, multinationals, and domestic and international developers, but we also advise lenders and the public sector. Our work regularly involves projects in Continental Europe, Africa, Middle East as well as the UK.
There are also plenty of opportunities for you to get involved in pro bono work and we have an established pro bono programme which our lawyers are actively encouraged to participate in which means you will collaborate with others across the firm as well as a range of pro bono clients.
Our core UK Real Estate Transactional team is made up of 5 Partners, 2 Directors and 28 Lawyers.  The team is non-hierarchical.
What you will be responsible for
As a lawyer at Clifford Chance your remit will be to apply your full knowledge of the law within your specialist area by identifying legal issues, drafting and advising clients.  We have an extensive education programme, but you will also be expected to be proactive in ensuring that your legal knowledge and technical expertise is up to date.  You will collaborate in knowledge initiatives for the Firm.
You can expect to be involved in:
• the drafting, negotiation and analysis of both direct real estate and corporate real estate transaction documentation (including share purchase agreements), joint venture documentation,
• development work;
• landlord/tenant documentation;
• providing real estate advice and input on Finance and Corporate support matters including reviewing certificates of title and providing real estate specific input on SPAs and loan documents.
You will be working closely with Partners and other Lawyers, helping to develop more junior lawyers, and will have a high proportion of client contact.
As a senior lawyer in our team, you will be expected to take a lead associate role, often managing transactions and/or teams of lawyers, often across multiple practice areas and/or jurisdictions; or working as a real estate specialist supporting a wider team of lawyers from across the London office and/or the wider network
There is a clear transactional bias to our work and our lawyers are required to involve themselves in business development and the management and organisation of teams of clients, lawyers and professional advisers.  You will utilise client focus initiatives to understand and drive service levels to meet client needs.
Managing matters with a disciplined practice is key, including adhering to matter opening and conflicts clearance processes.
We have a wide range of tools and support services available and you will be expected to utilise "Best Delivery" tools and AI where applicable: e.g. Legora, Orbital WitnessCoPilot, templates, Legal Support Centre, Resource Management, Legal Project Managers and Matter Balance Reports.
We encourage all of our lawyers to take charge of their own development and you will be expected to complete any mandatory and relevant skills, risk and legal training.

Qualifications
Your experience
• You will have Senior Real Estate experience, gained at a City firm, or at an overseas common law practice with a highly regarded profile and a good grounding in real estate as an asset class.
• Ideally you will have corporate real estate experience, but this is not essential - we are primarily interested in a genuine commitment to being a real estate lawyer first and foremost and interest in working across different industry sectors and asset classes, however, should be open to developing your skills over time to include corporate real estate.
• You will naturally be able to demonstrate excellent document drafting skills.  You should also demonstrate strong communication and analytical skills, along with a high level of commercial awareness and will have had strong exposure of collaborating with multi-disciplinary teams.
• It is crucial that you can demonstrate an appetite for developing client relationships and thought leadership.
• A strong academic history is essential.

Additional Information
How we will support you
From your first day with us, you will have varied opportunities to continuously grow and development your skills and knowledge. From formal training, informal coaching and mentoring through to skills-based and technical training and on the job learning.

About This Job
We are seeking an Integrations engineer to join our team and help create a world-class unified API experience for our customers. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in building integrations with various tools via APIs and a keen interest in exploring new technologies and platforms.
As an Integrations Engineer at StackOne, you will play a crucial role in driving the expansion of our platform's capabilities. You will work to understand our customer’s unique needs and collaborate with the rest of the engineering team to add support for new integrations within the StackOne unified API. This is an opportunity to be at the forefront of innovation, enabling seamless connections between the diverse range of tools and services that power today's SaaS ecosystem.
Responsibilities
• Help scope & gather requirements to understand customers’ integration needs
• Collaborate with the engineering team to design and develop new integrations and capabilities for the StackOne unified API
• Research and explore various tools and platforms to identify opportunities for expanding StackOne's integration capabilities
• Continuously improve the performance, reliability, and scalability of existing integrations
• Provide technical support and guidance to customers during the integration process, ensuring a smooth and positive experience
• Contribute to the development of integration-related documentation, guidelines, and best practices
• Stay up-to-date with industry trends and emerging technologies in the API and integration space

Qualifications
Requirements
• 2+ years of experience in software engineering with a focus on web applications
• Prior professional experience using Typescript and/or Node.js
• Experience interacting with APIs
• Solid communication and collaboration skills
• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills

Additional Information
⚡️ Our Stack
As one of the first senior engineering hires in the company, you will have a lot of freedom and agency to choose and work with the technology you love. Our tech stack includes:
• Infra & monitoring: AWS (ECS, Postgres), Datadog, Sentry…
• Languages & Frameworks: Typescript (Node.js), NestJs, Rails
• Other day-to-day Tools: Notion, Slack, Jira, GitHub, and more
🚀 Product
Our integration platform is unique for SaaS because:
• It’s easy and fast. To add dozens of integrations, you only need to integrate once with our unified API and we take care of the rest. This is way faster, cheaper, and more reliable than building every integration to each tool one at a time (it can take weeks/months per integration).
• We enrich and standardize APIs: Don’t worry about the headache of figuring out how every tool’s API works. We add features that don’t exist out of the box (like using filters in your query or triggering a webhook when data changes) and make all APIs behave in the same consistent way. It’s easier and better to go through StackOne than to connect to the tools directly.
• Extreme security and privacy: We will soon be SOC2 certified, we have data residency options for GDPR compliance, and more features to protect your customers’ data.

NEW GROUND WON’T BREAK ITSELF.
Every day our teams help people in businesses and communities to do what is right and achieve their goals.

Our teams bring together deep sector knowledge with technical expertise to deliver internal audit, technology risk and assurance services to FTSE 100 and large, complex international organisations.
The Data, AI & Analytics team provides audit, assurance and advisory services to Grant Thornton clients in the UK and internationally. A look into the role
As an Assistant Manager within BRS, you will:
• Take day-to-day responsibility for delivering client engagements focused on data & AI, technology risk, managing fieldwork from planning through to reporting, working closely with a Manager or above.
• Support the planning of engagements, including risk assessments, scoping, terms of reference and audit programmes, and lead planning on smaller or less complex assignments.
• Manage the financials of your engagements, including maintaining fee and cost forecasts, monitoring WIP, raising invoices in a timely manner and minimising debt, providing regular updates to your Manager.
• Perform and take responsibility for fieldwork, including data analysis, control testing, discovery exercises and maturity assessments, and review work completed by Associates, ensuring it is completed in line with Grant Thornton methodologies and quality standards, with sufficient and appropriate evidence to support conclusions.
• Apply your growing expertise in data and AI assurance, to identify risks, generate insight and shape practical, proportionate recommendations for clients.
• Support the presentation of reports and findings to client stakeholders, translating technical work into clear, business-relevant conclusions.
• Provide on-the-job coaching and feedback to Associates, supporting their technical and professional development.
• Begin to build your internal and external network, identifying cross-service line (XLOS) opportunities, and supporting proposals and new business pitches.
• Contribute to the continued development of the practice’s data and AI assurance methodology, tools and propositions, including the use of automation and AI in internal audit delivery.
• Build strong working relationships with clients and colleagues, demonstrating professionalism, curiosity and a commitment to quality in all interactions.
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as an Assistant Manager with a focus on data and AI assurance, the minimum criteria you’ll need includes:
• A professional qualification (CISA, AAIA, ACA, CA, ACCA, IIA etc.), or working towards one, with experience of delivering audit and assurance engagements.

Job title:
Functional Specialist – Part Time - Midlands
Job Description:
What we offer
•

Excellent training and ongoing support – be part of our valued team where wellbeing is prioritised.

10% of Salary Bonus scheme (based on quality and performance).

Hybrid working – home and clinic based.

Watch this short video to find out more https://capita.wistia.com/medias/2spl0ey4a9
Other benefits
•
HCPC/NMC fees paid and full revalidation support.
•
15 weeks’ full maternity, adoption and shared parental pay.
•
Company pension, life assurance and Cycle2Work scheme.
•
Discounts across retail, travel, technology and wellbeing.
•
Free access to Headspace (for you and up to 5 others).
•
A paid volunteering day each year.
•
Ongoing training, development and clear career pathways.
•
25 days’ holiday (rising to 27 with service) pro rata with the option to buy more up to 5 days.
What you’ll do in this role:
•
Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
•
Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.
•
Write detailed evidence-based reports to support the DWP/DfC in making informed and objective decisions - no treatment or diagnosis required.
•
Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.

Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.

•
Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
•
Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

•
NMC registered Nurse (RGN, RMN or RNLD) or HCPC registered paramedic, occupational therapist or physiotherapist with a valid PIN and no current restrictions

Minimum of one year’s post-registration experience.
•
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
•
Ability to produce clear, accurate and detailed reports.
•
Comfortable working quickly to meet structured targets.
•
Good IT skills including Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn new systems while working remotely.
•
excellent observational and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper.
•
A driving licence or access to transport for assessment centre working.
