Job Description
Overview
Leading the edge of transformation.
Join our organisation, where we have a huge variety of projects on-the-go at any one time. So when you start this role with us, it could take your career wherever your interests lie. You'll find everyone here is willing to pitch in and help because we all want you to succeed, and we're ready to help you grow.
When it comes to living your life, we want you to get the most out of it. So talk to us about all our flexible and remote working policies that can support your personal priorities. Also, ask us about some of our recent pledges for Women's Equality, as well as being a 'Disability Confident' and 'Inclusive Employer.'
As a Cyber Security Consultant, you’ll play a pivotal role in protecting Aerospace, Defence and CNI/OT clients from evolving cyber threats. You’ll work on projects that shape national security, working alongside industry experts in a supportive, innovative environment. We offer clear pathways for career advancement, and professional development, and this role will suit a recently qualified professional who is looking to take their career to the next level and provide real world benefit to clients. In return, we offer a challenging and rewarding role, career development, an empowered and supportive working environment with a competitive reward package. We invest in your professional growth through certifications, training and leadership pathways. You will work on ‘business as usual’, technical refresh, and new project environments, applying technical knowledge and innovative thinking. You will help clients establish robust security governance, perform risk assessments, and deploy effective security controls and solutions aligned with business risk appetite.
The successful candidate will be a knowledgeable, enthusiastic and conscientious individual who has the relevant Information Assurance and Security qualifications, and experience in working in either Defence or CNI/OT. If you have strong cyber security fundamentals and are keen to develop expertise in Defence or CNI/OT, we’ll support you with training and certifications. You will work on a range of client facing projects, large and small, but will also be expected to contribute to winning new business and managing delivery. Projects are likely to involve working on client sites, (although hybrid working allows us to be flexible), and may involve travel across the UK and, occasionally overseas.
Your role
Client Delivery-
• Provide cyber security advice and guidance for clients in various environments.
• Lead and deliver risk assessments, security governance, and deployment of effective security controls tailored to client needs.
• Develop, review and maintain security related artefacts, policies and procedures to ensure compliance and best practice.
• Manage multiple projects concurrently, balancing business and client priorities.
• Deliver high-quality work under pressure and to tight deadlines, ensuring stakeholder expectations are met.
Technical Leadership-
• Apply technical security knowledge creatively to solve cyber security challenges.
• Assist in fostering a culture of continuous improvement within the security team.
• Articulate cyber security concepts and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Business Development-
• Assist with the identification of new business opportunities, contributing to proposals and client engagement.
• Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, stakeholders, and team members.
About you
• Experience of delivering technical cyber security consultancy in multi-disciplined environments, with proven ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
• Background in information assurance, including developing Information Security Management Systems (ISMS), conducting risk assessments, and deploying appropriate security controls.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders at all levels. Strong organisational skills, with experience managing multiple projects and tasks concurrently.
• Ability to deliver security outcomes to tight deadlines while maintaining quality and managing stakeholder expectations. Willingness and flexibility to travel throughout the UK (and occasionally overseas) as required.
• Relevant professional certifications (e.g., ISO27000, CISMP, CISM, CISSP) are highly desirable. Solid understanding of ‘Secure by Design’ methodology. Commitment to ongoing professional development and willingness to learn new frameworks and technologies.
• Experience in the UK Defence sector, including knowledge of MoD security policies and processes (e.g., HMG Information Assurance Policies, Security Policy Framework, JSP440, JSP604/JSP453).
• Experience conducting and managing security assurance and accreditation activities for Defence capabilities or experience delivering cyber security consultancy in OT environments (e.g., energy, utilities, transportation).
• Experience in segmenting and securing industrial OT/ICS networks. Any Control & Instrumentation background would be an added advantage. Familiarity with OT cyber security standards or regulatory frameworks (e.g., IEC 62443, NIST CSF, NIS Regulations, HSE OG-0086).
• Relevant OT cyber security qualifications (e.g., GICSP, IEC/ISA 62443). Membership of recognised security professional bodies (e.g., IISP, IS2, BCS, CIISEC).
• Ability to create client policies and procedures to meet corporate and regulatory requirements in OT environments. Experience selecting and deploying appropriate technology in live CNI environments.
Reward & benefits
Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career. Enjoy competitive salaries, employee rewards and a brilliant range of benefits you can tailor to suit your own health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle choices. Make the most of a myriad of opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise. And combine our hybrid working culture and flexible holiday allowances to balance a great job and fulfilling personal life.
Be rewarded. Find out more.

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

King & Spalding is a leading global law firm with a commitment to excellence, innovation, and the seamless delivery of legal services. We harness innovative technology and exceptional talent to meet the complex needs of our clients in a fast-paced and dynamic legal landscape.
The Tax Manager (VAT) owns the day-to-day delivery of the Firm's indirect tax compliance activities across multiple jurisdictions, including Europe, APAC, and the Middle East. The role is accountable for maintaining compliance calendars, directing return preparation, completing or overseeing substantive reviews, coordinating external advisors, leading responses to indirect tax audits and inquiries, supervising the VAT Analyst, and ensuring that filings are accurate, complete, timely, and fully documented. The successful candidate will be a hands-on VAT compliance professional who takes end-to-end ownership of recurring filing obligations, drives issues through resolution, and leads practical improvements to processes, controls, technology, and the continued build-out of the Firm's indirect tax operations function.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Manage preparation, review, and submission of VAT/GST returns across applicable jurisdictions.
• Manage European Sales Listings, Intrastat filings, and other periodic indirect tax reporting obligations.
• Own the Firm's VAT compliance calendar and ensure filing deadlines and submission requirements are met.
• Review supporting workpapers, account reconciliations, data extracts, and compliance documentation prepared by the VAT Analyst or external advisors.
• Maintain organized compliance records, audit trails, filing confirmations, and supporting documentation.
• Monitor VAT legislative and administrative developments that may affect the Firm's compliance obligations.
• Evaluate the operational impact of regulatory changes and coordinate implementation of required filing or process updates.
• Provide practical VAT guidance in response to routine queries from Billing, Accounts Payable, Finance, and local office teams.
• Escalate complex technical matters, recurring risks, or significant compliance concerns to the Indirect Tax Operations Manager.
• Support VAT registrations, deregistrations, and changes to existing registrations as the Firm's obligations evolve.
• Manage recurring interactions with external VAT advisors and service providers.
• Coordinate information requests, filing deliverables, filing reviews, and advisor follow-up items.
• Coordinate responses to tax authority inquiries, VAT audits, and related compliance reviews.
• Monitor advisor deliverables and escalate delays, quality concerns, or unresolved technical issues.
• Support development of advisor governance procedures and filing review protocols.
• Lead, supervise, mentor, and develop the VAT Analyst, with accountability for effective day-to-day performance and professional growth.
• Set priorities, assign work, manage capacity, and hold team members accountable for accurate, timely, and well-documented deliverables.
• Review work, provide timely and constructive feedback, and deliver technical coaching on VAT filings, reconciliations, documentation, and routine query handling.
• Own the onboarding, training, and continued development of additional indirect tax operations team members as the function grows.
• Establish and reinforce clear expectations for ownership, quality, timeliness, documentation, communication, and escalation discipline.
• Support e-invoicing and real-time reporting initiatives by providing compliance input, data validation, testing support, and issue resolution.
• Contribute to process documentation, compliance playbooks, checklists, desk procedures, and control improvements.
• Identify opportunities to improve compliance efficiency, data quality, and filing consistency.
• Support tax residency certificate requests, withholding tax documentation collection, and related tax operations activities as needed.
• Participate in special projects and operational initiatives led by the Indirect Tax Operations Manager.
QUALIFICATIONS:
• 8+ years of VAT or indirect tax compliance experience, ideally within a multinational organization, professional services firm, or law firm environment.
• Strong practical knowledge of VAT/GST returns, European Sales Listings, Intrastat reporting, VAT registrations, and related compliance requirements.
• Experience managing multi-jurisdictional filing obligations and advisor relationships.
• Experience supporting VAT audits, tax authority inquiries, or compliance reviews.
• Strong Excel and data management skills.
• Excellent organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and competing priorities across jurisdictions.
• A proactive and solutions-oriented approach, with the confidence to take ownership of day-to-day compliance activities and drive issues through to resolution.
• Interest in e-invoicing, tax technology, automation, and process improvement initiatives.
• ATT, CTA, ACA, ACCA, or equivalent qualification, or progress toward qualification, is preferred.
• Strong VAT compliance judgment and attention to detail.
• Ability to manage multiple filing deadlines and competing priorities across jurisdictions.
• Strong organizational skills and the ability to maintain disciplined compliance documentation.
• Comfort working with large datasets, spreadsheets, reconciliations, and compliance reporting tools.
• Practical communication style and ability to work effectively with Finance, Billing, Accounts Payable, local offices, external advisors, and tax colleagues.
• Proactive, solutions-oriented approach with willingness to take ownership of day-to-day compliance activities.
• Ability to supervise and develop less experienced team members.
The Firm offers a generous total compensation package with annual bonus in recognition of individual merit-based performance. Eligible employees may participate in King & Spalding’s comprehensive benefit program, including private medical insurance with Bupa, life assurance (4x salary), critical illness insurance (2x salary) and income protection insurance, 7% firm pension contribution, gym membership/wellness allowance contribution, Employee Assistance Programme, season ticket loan, cycle to work scheme and 25 days annual holiday.
King & Spalding LLP (K&S) is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all applicants and employees in full compliance with all local laws prohibiting discrimination, including on the basis of race, religion and belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, marital status, pregnancy status or any other status protected by applicable law.

The Position
This position is designed for an experienced professional with a demonstrated track record of both rigorous program and project execution and the change management required to drive solution adoption within the Biotech/Pharma landscape.
Disciplined program and project management, milestone tracking, and active execution are core to this role - as is the stakeholder alignment, change and communication strategies required to embed outcomes into sustainable, "business as usual" operations. Both disciplines are essential to realizing the full value of any initiative we deliver.
In this role, you will bridge technical, operational, and business boundaries - combining hands-on delivery expertise with change management principles to ensure initiatives hit key milestones, overcome operational friction and adoption barriers, and realize their intended business value.
We welcome applications from accomplished professionals with a strong background in program/project and change management - and a demonstrated ability to operate credibly across both disciplines. Recognizing our need to scale capabilities in an increasingly data-driven environment, we are specifically interested in candidates who can bridge the gap between technical teams—including software engineers and data scientists—and business execution and solution adoption. Experience or a strong understanding of Data Science and Analytics projects, coupled with demonstrated digital curiosity and broad knowledge in areas like Agentic AI, will be highly valued as a critical asset for success in this role.
As Business & Program Management Leader your responsibilities will include but not be limited to:
Project Execution, Delivery and Governance
• Scope, plan, and execute project roadmaps and ensure solutions are adopted to drive intended value realization within the agreed timeframe and in an iterative manner.
• Ensure consistent application of project delivery standards, managing the day-to-day "mechanics" of delivery, cross-functional coordination, and deliverable development.
• Contribute to and manage team processes for development of critical deliverables.
• Maintain accurate plans and program/project documentation, ensuring that risks and issues are promptly captured, tracked, and communicated.
• Actively capture, track, and mitigate operational, timeline, and execution risks; ensure risk registers are updated and escalations are managed promptly.
• Prepare clear data updates and progress metrics to support executive governance bodies, ensuring decision-making is grounded in accurate progress tracking.
• Optimize team performance by establishing team norms, facilitating productive decision-making, and simplifying complex cross-functional workflows.
Business Adoption & Value Realization
• Design and deploy solution adoption frameworks to ensure program/project deliverables are seamlessly embedded into daily operational workflows across impacted business units.
• Consider the "voice of the end-user" during planning; perform impact assessments, map user journeys, and proactively address adoption barriers or resistance.
• Establish and monitor user proficiency, adoption rates, and value-sustainment outcomes in close partnership with Project Leads and Sponsors.

We’re looking for an AI Solutions Technical Engineering Manager to lead the delivery of AI- and data-enabled products and platforms from early shaping through to measurable outcomes in production. You’ll operate at the intersection of engineering leadership, AI delivery, and stakeholder alignment, turning ambiguous ideas into structured plans, unblocking teams, and ensuring solutions are operationally viable.
You will work across domain teams in a federated model, bringing clarity around ownership, interfaces, and accountability. This is a senior role for someone who can drive innovation while delivering under tight timelines and high expectations.
The role
You will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams (AI/ML, data, software, platform) to deliver AI capabilities that are trusted, adopted, and production-grade.
Day to day, you're splitting time between running the team and doing real technical work alongside them — reviewing designs and code, prototyping when it's faster than explaining, and making the calls on deployment, routing, evaluation, and monitoring for our LLM and ML systems. That includes when to use semantic routing versus static routing, when OpenRouter-style multi-provider setups make sense, and how Claude and other models stay integrated cleanly across different tech stacks rather than bolted on inconsistently.
You'll own technical direction of our text-to-SQL platform. You're also the technical backstop for agent and MCP work: tool-use design, orchestration patterns, and knowing when MCP is the right call versus overkill.
On models, you decide whether a problem needs fine-tuning or whether better prompting, retrieval, or routing gets there faster and cheaper; backed by real evaluation data, not intuition.
Beyond that, you keep what we ship production-grade — secure, observable, cost-sensible, reliable. You manage the people side properly too: coaching, growth, honest feedback. And you represent AI delivery to senior stakeholders, staying calm and credible under tight timelines and open questions.
What you’ll be doing
•
Someone who has actually built and shipped AI/ML systems themselves, recently nough that they can still read and write code and hold their own in a design review
•
Real depth on LLM systems — RAG, agentic architectures, tool use, evaluation, guardrails, model lifecycle — not just familiarity with the terms
•
Hands-on experience with multi-model or multi-provider setups — routing (semantic routers, OpenRouter or equivalents), fallback strategies, and cost/latency trade-offs across providers.
•
You're also the technical backstop for our KAIT platform - our LibreChat-based internal AI tool, covering MCP gateway architecture, agent orchestration, and integrations across Confluence, Jira, Teams, and ClickHouse.
•
Practical experience with MCP-based integrations and agent orchestration, including the judgment to know when an agentic approach is overkill
•
A working understanding of fine-tuning versus prompt/retrieval-based approaches, and the evaluation rigor to justify the choice with data
•
Experience leading a small senior team where you were still the most technical person in the room, or close to it
•
Comfortable making architecture decisions without a clear playbook, and confident enough to defend them on technical merit
•
Solid production engineering fundamentals - AWS, Kubernetes, CI/CD, observability - enough to have an opinion, not necessarily to build it yourself day to day
•
Genuinely plugged into what's happening in AI right now, and able to tell the difference between a real capability shift and a marketing claim
•
Communicates well enough to make technical trade-offs land with non-technical senior stakeholders, without dumbing anything down
•
Own delivery of AI workloads and AI-enabled products end-to-end: from discovery through build, launch, and iteration
•
Convert loosely defined ideas into delivery plans, milestones, and measurable outcomes
What success looks like
•
AI ideas actually make it to production — not stuck in prototype limbo — and you can point to real business impact, not just "it's live"
•
The team ships fast without cutting corners on evaluation, security, or cost — because you're close enough to the work to catch problems before they become production incidents
•
Your engineers see you as a technical peer they'd escalate a hard problem to, not just someone tracking their tickets
•
Text-2-SQL, the agent/MCP work, and model integrations stay reliable and well-governed as they scale — not held together by one person's tribal knowledge
•
When trade-offs get hard — speed vs. quality, build vs. buy, fine-tune vs. prompt — you make the call, back it with data, and stakeholders trust it even when the timeline is brutal
Experience and capabilities (essential)
•
Proven experience leading engineering delivery for data-heavy, AI-enabled, or platform products
•
Strong understanding of modern AI concepts: ML systems, LLMs, data dependencies, evaluation, and operational risks
•
Track record managing complex deliveries across multiple teams and stakeholders
•
Comfortable operating in federated/domain-oriented environments with shared ownership
•
Excellent communication: able to align senior stakeholders and guide teams through ambiguity
•
Solid grasp of production engineering fundamentals: cloud, reliability, security, monitoring, CI/CD
Technical environment

Cloud: AWS / Azure / GCP

AI/ML delivery: model deployment, MLOps/LLMOps, monitoring, iteration
•
Platform foundations: Kubernetes (EKS/AKS), CI/CD, GitOps concepts
•
Observability: metrics, logs, tracing; dashboards and alerting disciplines
•
Architecture: APIs, microservices, event-driven systems; data pipelines
Desirable

Delivery experience in regulated or high-stakes environments (financial services, gambling/gaming compliance)

Working knowledge of AI governance and where regulation like the EU AI Act is heading

• Quantifying the financial impact of alleged breaches of contract or duty, including lost profits, diminution in value and business interruption losses across a wide range of commercial disputes
• Advising clients involved in transaction disputes, including post-acquisition disputes, warranty and indemnity claims and expert determinations
• Preparing and reviewing contentious business valuations in the context of litigation, arbitration and other dispute resolution proceedings

• Experience of managing teams in delivering disputes or valuation workstreams
• Flexibility to work across a range of industries, sectors and dispute types

LSEG already reaches the desks that need models: through our APIs, our Excel integrations, and the workflows clients use every day. Modeling Solutions turns that reach into a distribution channel for third-party models, so a client can consume an external model in the same place, and the same way, they consume everything else from us.
The business has three pillars: Model Distribution, a marketplace connecting model providers with the institutions that consume them; Model Hosting, the infrastructure clients use to run models in production; and AI Model Risk Management, governance and monitoring sold as a differentiated product.

Discovery with providers and institutional buyers, prioritization against real engineering constraints, and the sequencing calls between Distribution, Hosting, and MRM-AI. Shape Hosting into something clients want to run on, and build MRM-AI into a product differentiated enough to open accounts on its own.

• State estimation and sensor fusion development.

• Technical risk identification and mitigation.
• Development and exploitation of artificial intelligence

What You’ll bring

• Inertial navigation systems
• GNSS/GPS technologies
• Coordinate transformations and reference frames
• Error propagation and uncertainty analysis
• Sensor fusion techniques
• Experience with Kalman Filters or related estimation approaches.
• Experience using MATLAB and Simulink for modelling and simulation.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to communicate complex technical concepts effectively.
Desirable

• Experience developing navigation systems for defence, aerospace or autonomous platforms.

• Multi-sensor fusion architectures, multi-modal and multiple-hypothesis filtering
• Visual-Inertial Navigation
• SLAM techniques

Big responsibility. Personal support. That’s Beyond the Ordinary.

The opportunity to build your experience, confidence and career without having to do it alone.

We are actively expanding the Crypto & Security Competence Centre (CCC&S) at NXP and we have new opportunities in our team for digital verification engineers working on next-generation security technologies such as:
• Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) IP
• Secure SoC subsystems, including next-generation roots of trust

Driven Verification – What You’ll Be Part Of
In this role, you will contribute to a step-change in verification capability through:
• AI-driven verification automation – reducing regression effort while maintaining full coverage
• Intelligent debug and analysis – accelerating bug discovery and root-cause identification
• Automated test and vPlan generation – improving consistency and reducing human error
We are also actively developing advanced capabilities including:
• AI-assisted RTL understanding and test explanation
• Conversational debug interfaces for waveform and design interaction
• AI-driven coverage closure and test prioritization
This is not a future vision—this transformation is already underway within CCC&S workflows.
What You’ll Be Doing
As a key member of our growing team, you will:
• Lead the verification of advanced PQC and security IP, tackling complex, security-focused design challenges
• Define and drive verification strategy, leveraging AI and automation to enhance productivity and quality
• Architect and scale SystemVerilog/UVM verification environments for IP and subsystem-level validation
• Champion Constrained Random and Metrics-Driven Verification (MDV) methodologies
• Own and drive coverage closure, using data-driven insights for high-confidence sign-off
• Develop SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) for protocol checking and early defect detection
• Collaborate closely with design and architecture teams to influence verification from early stages
• Mentor and support engineers, contributing to a high-performing and forward-looking team culture
Why This Role Stands Out
• Work on cutting-edge cryptography technologies critical to future cybersecurity
• Help define how AI transforms verification workflows and methodologies
• Join a growing organisation where your input shapes tools, processes, and technical direction
• Take ownership of high-visibility, complex projects from concept to silicon
Your Profile
• BSc., or MSc., degree in Electronics or Electrical Engineering.
• Strong hands-on experience with SystemVerilog for testbench development and verification.
• Proven expertise in UVM (Universal Verification Methodology), including component creation, sequences, drivers, monitors, and scoreboards.
• Solid understanding and practical use of Constrained Random Verification techniques.
• Experience with Metrics‑Driven Verification, including functional coverage and verification planning.
• Ability to write SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) for protocol and design checking.
• Demonstrated success in achieving Coverage Closure across functional and code coverage metrics.
• Experience analysing coverage results and refining test strategies to close gaps.
• Strong debugging skills across simulations and complex verification environments.
• Knowledge of Formal Verification methods would be advantageous.
If you're excited by the opportunity to work at the intersection of hardware, security, and AI, and want to contribute to technologies that will define the next decade, we invite you to apply!

We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact. Here, your curiosity fuels progress, your voice shapes innovation, and your ambition helps redefine what’s possible within science and learning. We are a culture that obsesses over impact, challenges, and drives what’s next to power infinite possibilities for our customers, colleagues and society at large.
About the Role:
About the role
We're building the systems that turn one of the world's largest scientific corpora into research intelligence. That means production NLP pipelines running over millions of journal articles, extracting entities, classifications, claim tuples, and summaries optimized for use by downstream agentic applications. We're looking for a senior data scientist to own domain-specific content modeling work end to end, from the eval set through the pipeline stage that ships it.
You'll join a small, senior team where data scientists own their models in production. You'll write the code, own the evaluations, ship the changes, and stay accountable for the outcomes. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to see their models through to real users in a rapidly evolving market.
What you'll do
•
Design and build NLP enrichment pipelines that extract entities, classifications, claims, and summaries from scientific full-text at scale.
•
Compare NLP approaches to extraction and enrichment against LLM-based approaches, and pick the right tool for each task. That means putting traditional NLP (NER, sequence labeling, classification), embedding-based retrieval, LLM prompting, and fine-tuned smaller models on the same table, and defending each choice with evaluation, cost, and operational tradeoffs. This is a core part of the job, not an occasional exercise.
•
Own evaluation. Build the golden sets in consultation with SMEs and vendors, choose the metrics, and make productive tradeoffs between speed, quality, and cost.
•
Contribute to agentic AI application work: tool-using systems that reason over the enriched corpus, where your NLP and evaluation background will shape how the agent grounds and defends its answers.
•
Work directly with editors, product managers, and engineers. Bring the modeling perspective into product decisions, and translate stakeholder pushback into concrete modeling work.
What you'll bring
•
Strong NLP background across modern (LLMs, transformers, embeddings, retrieval) and classical (NER, classification, sequence labeling) approaches. You've built evaluations and learned from the results.
•
Clean python.  You are comfortable in exploratory notebooks and production repositories, and an engineer taking over a modeling output from you has a good head start.
•
A habit of comparing approaches and choosing the right one for the task. You can defend "prompt a large LLM" and "train a small classifier on 2,000 labels" with equal seriousness, back the choice with an eval and a cost estimate, and know what to do when performance drifts.
Nice to have
•
Experience working with scientific or scholarly text.
•
Familiarity with AWS (S3, Batch, Lambda, SageMaker) and Parquet or Iceberg data lake patterns.
•
Experience running LLMs under real cost and latency budgets in production.
•
Some exposure to agentic AI applications: tool use, multi-step reasoning, guardrails, and evaluation of trajectories rather than single-turn outputs.
Why us
We publish some of the world's most-read research, and we're now in a rare position: applying modern AI to a corpus of trusted scientific knowledge that spans two centuries. Researchers will use the systems you build here to move faster and get closer to the answers they came for. That's the work: from knowledge to impact.
We power infinite possibilities.
For more than 200 years, we've transformed knowledge into discoveries that shape the world. Today, our global team of innovators, creators, and experts is driving what's next in science, education, and publishing—creating impact that reaches everywhere.
We're not just observers of progress. We're the ones accelerating scientific breakthroughs, advancing learning, and sparking innovation that redefines entire fields and improves lives.
Here, your talent matters. Your ideas have room to grow. And your work creates breakthroughs that can change everything.

Valuable (but not essential):

Big ambitions. Personal investment. That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Ready to start your career, learn by doing and see where your ambitions could take you? Welcome to the Audit School Leaver Apprenticeship at BDO.
The programme starts on Monday, 20th September 2027, for an organisation-wide induction (you need to be able to attend).
We’re the only UK mid-market organisation with more than £1bn in turnover and 8,000 people. Audit at BDO gives you the chance to get involved and build experience from day one. Our Audit teams work across specialist areas including Pension Audit, Public Sector, Not-for-Profit, Financial Services and Technology Risk Assurance, giving you the chance to learn how different organisations work from the inside out.

It’s a place to turn big ambitions into a career, with people personally invested in your growth from the start.
A bit about the Technology Risk Assurance team
Audit at BDO gives you the chance to take on meaningful work early in your career. We’re the only UK mid-market organisation with more than £1bn in turnover and 8,000 people. That means you get the scale and breadth of a major professional services business, while working with clients where your contribution can make a real difference.
We have roles within our Data Analytics and IT controls teams.
What does the TRA controls team do?
The Technology Risk Assurance Controls team helps the audit team identify and assess risks associated with the client's finance applications. We focus on IT systems and processes related to access, change management and automated interfaces between systems. When we identify weaknesses in the client IT environment, we provide recommendations to management to help them strengthen processes and controls. We also work closely with the financial audit team to explain the risks arising from IT that impact our audit approach and may require additional audit testing of financial statement integrity.
Key responsibilities include:
-IT General Controls testing over the financial applications
-Cyber Security Risk Assessments
-Database and Operating Systems controls testing
-Assessment of automated controls operated by the business
What does the TRA Data team do?
The TRA Data team uses data analytics to support audits by examining entire populations of financial data, rather than relying solely on traditional sample-based testing. By combining technology, data analysis and audit expertise, we help provide efficient, high-quality assurance across a range of financial statement areas.
Key responsibilities include:
-Exploring and analysing data to help understand how businesses operate and identify potential risks using tools such as Alteryx, Databricks, Python, SQL, SAS, amongst others
-Checking and validating financial information to support the audit process
-Working closely with colleagues across audit teams to solve problems and deliver successful outcomes
-Presenting insights in a clear and engaging way to help teams focus on key areas of risk, including building visualisations and dashboards
As for you
You’re curious, resilient and ready to learn. You enjoy solving problems, thinking things through and getting involved.
You don’t need to arrive with all the answers. Bring your ambition and willingness to learn, and we’ll give you opportunities to build your experience, confidence and skills from there.
Join us in one of the following areas;
Controls – Reading

We’ll keep you updated at each stage and share resources to help you prepare. And just so you know: we don’t use AI in any part of our candidate screening process. Every application is reviewed by a real person.

Our benefits are designed to support your life in and outside of work, with options including additional leave, gym membership and employee discounts, alongside pension, health and wellbeing support and a range of protection benefits.

£26,615 - £28,275 dependable on location.

Starting your career is a big step. At BDO, you’ll get the chance to learn by doing, work with clients and build strong foundations for where you want to go next.
You’ll bring the big ambitions. You’ll have people around you investing in your learning, confidence and development from the start.

Lithium Battery Safety Management

Job Description:
Business Development Manager - Hellenic Systems Ltd
Location:  Home-based, anywhere in the UK, with regular travel to customer sites and periodic visits to our Essex head office
About Hellenic Systems
Founded in 1988, Hellenic Systems Ltd builds the systems that run the factory floor. Our software tells operators what to make and in what order, records what actually happened, and proves it to an auditor afterwards. The industry name for this is Manufacturing Execution Systems, or MES: the layer that sits between a company’s business systems and the machinery and people producing the goods. We design and manufacture the hardware that goes with it as well.
We are UK-based and serve over 130 sites across the UK and Europe. Our roots are in food manufacturing, particularly meat and poultry, and we are now extending into any manufacturer with the same problem to solve. A large share of what we ship is built specifically for one customer, which is why our tagline, Built Around You, is meant literally.
Our three software products are CARCASE, our kill line and livestock system, FOPS, our Factory Order Processing System, and FORMIX, our recipe and formulation management system. Our hardware includes weigh scales, touch screen terminals, outer case marking systems, carcass data capture units and label printers.
Since 2023 we have been part of Vesta Software Group, which sits within Jonas Software, an operating group of Constellation Software Inc. Constellation is one of the largest acquirers of vertical market software businesses in the world.
We are also unusually far along with AI for a business our size. It is embedded in how we build software and how we work day to day, not run as a side project, and we expect everyone here to use it.
The Opportunity
FORMIX, our recipe and formulation management system, has been rebuilt as a new product and is our main new business push. It guides operators through ingredient weigh-up, enforces tolerances, captures batch and operator evidence, and connects to shop floor weighing and labelling hardware. The buyers are food and drink manufacturers who still run weigh-up on paper, spreadsheets or an awkward ERP screen, and who are under real pressure on allergen control, traceability and waste.
This is a new role. It exists to build and convert a new business pipeline that does not depend on our existing account base.
Job Summary
The Business Development Manager owns new business at Hellenic. The role is targeted on winning new named clients and new sites, starting with FORMIX and broadening into our wider software and hardware portfolio as the pipeline develops. It is a hunting role: self-generated prospecting, campaigns and networking, then running the opportunity through demonstration, proposal, negotiation and close, with support from our technical and commercial teams.
The BDM reports to the Head of Commercial and works alongside our Account Managers, who own existing customer relationships. Growth inside existing accounts stays with them. Anything genuinely new belongs to the BDM.
Key Responsibilities
1. New Business Generation
•
Win new named clients and new sites, principally for FORMIX in year one, broadening into CARCASE, FOPS, hardware and bespoke development as the pipeline matures.
•
Generate the majority of your own pipeline through outbound prospecting, cold calling, email and LinkedIn campaigns, trade events and industry networking. Marketing and referral leads will supplement this, not replace it.
•
Work the named FORMIX prospect list and the wider addressable market, including manufacturers outside our traditional meat and poultry base, such as bakery, dairy, ready meals, sauces, seasonings, flavourings and beverages.
•
Open the first opportunities in adjacent sectors as we extend the product into adjacent sectors, and feed what you learn back into product and pricing.
•
Qualify hard and early. We would rather have a smaller pipeline we believe in than a large one we do not.
2. Selling and Closing
•
Run the full sales cycle: discovery, on-site assessment, demonstration (in person and remote), proposal, commercial negotiation and close.
•
Build the business case in the customer’s language: reduced giveaway and waste, right first time batches, allergen control, audit-ready evidence and labour saved on the weigh-up line.
•
Prepare and present quotations and proposals that reflect our pricing model, including site-level and tiered packaging.
•
Present our solution accurately and never oversell what the product does. Where a requirement needs bespoke development, involve the technical team for scope.
•
Hand over cleanly to Projects and Support at the point of sale, including a written summary of what has been sold and what the customer expects.
3. Market, Product and Competitor Knowledge
•
Build and hold working knowledge of the FORMIX proposition and enough of the wider portfolio to spot an opportunity when a customer describes a problem.
•
Know the competition. Be able to explain where we win and where we do not.
•
Gather field intelligence on competitor pricing, bundling and contract terms.
•
Track sector trends, regulation and retailer or certification pressures (for example BRCGS) that create a reason for customers to act.
4. Pipeline, CRM and Reporting
•
Build and maintain a qualified pipeline of sufficient size and quality to deliver the agreed targets, with realistic close dates and values.
•
Keep CRM current and accurate. Every opportunity, activity, contact and next step is logged.
•
Report weekly on activity, pipeline movement and forecast, and present your numbers at commercial reviews.
•
Learn and follow the company sales guidelines and standard operating procedures, and help improve our proposal and correspondence templates as you go.
•
Use AI tools in your daily workflow: prospect and account research, first-draft proposals and follow-ups, call preparation and pipeline analysis. We will give you the tools and the training.
5. Working With the Team
•
Work with the Account Managers so that new business and account growth do not collide, and pass leads to them where an opportunity sits inside an existing relationship.
•
Work with Development, Projects and Support on solution scoping, demonstrations and delivery expectations.
•
Contribute to campaigns, marketing content, case studies and event planning.
•
Attend training to keep product, sector and sales skills current, and take part in team meetings and reviews.
•
Carry out other reasonable duties related to the promotion, sale and delivery of our products as directed by the management team.
Targets and Measures of Success
You will carry a personal new business target, set annually with the Head of Commercial and reviewed each quarter. It covers new order value, new recurring revenue and a minimum number of genuinely new clients, and it is supported by activity and pipeline coverage measures and by the quality of what you put into the CRM.

What you’ll bring
Entry Requirements

Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

Managing Consultant – Construction Environmental Manager
Make Your Mark at ERM
ERM is seeking an experienced and motivated Managing Consultant – Construction Environmental Manager to support the delivery of major infrastructure projects during the construction phase. This role offers the opportunity to be at the forefront of project delivery, providing on-site environmental leadership and ensuring construction activities are undertaken in compliance with environmental commitments, consent requirements, and regulatory obligations.
Working across sectors including electricity transmission and distribution, renewable energy, hydrogen, solar, and onshore wind, you will play a critical role in helping clients translate environmental commitments into practical construction controls, ensuring projects are delivered responsibly, sustainably, and in line with regulatory expectations.
As a senior member of the team, you will act as the environmental lead on site, working closely with construction teams, contractors, clients, environmental specialists, and regulators to manage environmental risk and drive a culture of environmental excellence throughout project delivery.
The Role
As a Construction Environmental Manager, you will lead environmental compliance and environmental management activities during construction. You will act as the primary environmental point of contact on-site, ensuring environmental requirements are effectively implemented, monitored, and communicated across all project activities.
You will work closely with project teams to identify environmental risks, resolve compliance issues, and ensure mitigation measures and monitoring commitments are delivered effectively throughout construction.
Key Responsibilities
•
Lead the delivery of Construction Environmental Manager services on major infrastructure and energy projects during construction.
•
Act as the primary environmental representative on-site, providing advice and support to construction teams, contractors, and project management personnel.
•
Ensure construction activities are undertaken in accordance with consent conditions, environmental permits, licences, approved management plans, and project commitments.
•
Support the implementation and management of Construction Environmental Management Plans (CEMPs) and associated topic-specific environmental management plans.
•
Monitor compliance with environmental commitments, mitigation measures, and legal obligations throughout the construction phase.
•
Conduct regular site inspections, compliance audits, and environmental monitoring activities to identify risks and drive continual improvement.
•
Lead investigations into environmental incidents, non-conformances, complaints, and near misses, ensuring appropriate corrective actions are implemented.
•
Maintain environmental compliance records and provide clear documentation demonstrating adherence to project requirements.
•
Support the management of environmental risks relating to areas such protected species, water quality, waste management, pollution prevention, noise, air quality, and biodiversity.
•
Deliver environmental inductions, toolbox talks, and awareness sessions to promote environmental best practice across the project workforce.
•
Coordinate environmental monitoring programmes and oversee the implementation of mitigation and enhancement measures.
•
Liaise effectively with clients, contractors, environmental specialists, regulators, and other stakeholders regarding environmental performance and compliance.
•
Prepare compliance reports, environmental performance dashboards, audit findings, and management updates for project leadership teams and regulators.
•
Support regulator inspections, client audits, and independent compliance reviews.
•
Mentor and support junior environmental professionals within project teams.
•
Contribute to business development activities, proposal preparation, and the continued growth of ERM’s construction environmental management services.
Why This Role Matters
Effective environmental management during construction is essential to delivering infrastructure projects safely, responsibly, and in compliance with regulatory requirements. As a Construction Environmental Manager, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring environmental commitments made during the consenting process are successfully implemented on the ground.
Your expertise will help clients reduce environmental risk, maintain programme certainty, foster positive stakeholder relationships, and demonstrate environmental leadership throughout construction. Through your work, you will contribute to the successful delivery of projects that support the transition to a more sustainable future.

•
Experience in construction environmental management, environmental compliance, environmental advisory, or project environmental delivery within the UK infrastructure sector.
•
Degree (or equivalent qualification) in Environmental Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Ecology, Engineering, or a related discipline.

Experience supporting or leading environmental management activities during the construction phase of major infrastructure projects.

Strong understanding of environmental legislation, regulatory compliance requirements, and environmental management systems.
